convergence.exportInvocation: pen interactive --in <file.pen> --out <scratch.pen>; execute({ input: 'Export(["<frameId>", ...], "png", "<dir>")' }) - default scale 2; the .pen MUST sit at its committed lane path so the relative library import (../../../design-system/in-progress/hemlock-library.lib.pen) and font URI (../../fonts/Heebo-VariableFont_wght.ttf) resolve. Re-export verified byte-deterministic across consecutive runs (all 17 frame hashes identical).
convergence.comparison: pixelmatch threshold 0.1, per-state budget 1.0% (dispatch default; tighter than the contract's story-vs-pen pixelThreshold 0.03). Targets = NORMALIZED prototype (never raw), contract root section.bc, Chromium headless-shell 145.0.7632.6 (playwright 1.58), deviceScaleFactor 2, network blocked, animations frozen, fonts ready, double-capture self-consistency all 17 states byte-identical. Heebo rendered from the same TTF the .pen references (pencil/designs/fonts/Heebo-VariableFont_wght.ttf, installed into fontconfig).
convergence.iterationNotes: Iteration 1 converged all 17 states at 0.004-0.192% (residual = cross-rasterizer text antialiasing; no state needed a fix round). Authoring used per-fontSize pen-vs-Chromium baseline calibration (pen quantizes the in-box baseline to integer px with lineHeight 1; offsets measured empirically per size via flat-cap H-glyph subpixel edge detection, weight-independent). default and static-print exports are byte-identical, matching the contract's identical-by-construction claim (design-rules 20).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: categorical series slot 1 (--cat1: bars, legend swatch 1, hover swatch 1)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Dispatch chart rule: series colors bind the defaultChartPalette roles IN SERIES ORDER, never primitives that happen to match the prototype's blues. Series 1 therefore renders priority color 1 (purple) - a deliberate, visible divergence from Bill's literal palette order. #3B82F6 exists in the system as color-04; hue-matching it was explicitly rejected.

Variable double-duty: --cat9 is both categorical slot 9 (never rendered in any contracted state) and the ramp's purple hue (rendered). Mapped by RENDERED role; Bill's value already equals color-01, so this is an identity injection. A slot-9 mapping (color-09 #C026D3) would silently recolor the ramp. Land stage must separate the ramp palette from the categorical slots (one variable namespace in the prototype).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: ramp full-strength blue (--accent: series 1 of ramp states, benchmark series 1)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: The ramp's blue steps ARE a single-hue sequential progression; seq-600 is the chart-fill token with the exact light value. Alternatives considered: sem-chartLineAction (line-chart role, same light value) and sem-background-action (non-chart).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: axis (baseline + tick text + category labels, --axis) and gridlines (--grid)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Design-rules 1 deliberately UNIFIES the baseline and tick text in one darker axis colour while gridlines sit back - Hemlock's existing vocabulary splits axis-line ($sem-borders-dark, taupe #DCD8CB) from tick text ($sem-text-meta, #5E5954) with no token owning either of Bill's values. Splitting one CSS variable into two roles is impossible without structural edits, so both roles got created semantic tokens with Bill's values (never-stop doctrine); the designer's adopt-vs-remap ruling is recorded as designGaps.

tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: hand-rolled SVG bar chart (plot + legend + info box + error box)
tokenJudgmentCalls.boundToken: (none - frames drawn from extracted prototype geometry)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: hemlock-library has component/BarChart, ChartAxisGrid, ChartTooltip, ChartLegend - all a different design (card chrome, 11px meta ticks, own layout) that cannot reproduce the executable spec's geometry (viewBox-scaled type, backer bars, tick text inside the plot, 60%-gap-cap bar math). Under the two-oracle split the .pen is the pixel oracle OF THIS prototype, so frames carry the prototype's exact rendered geometry with token paint; composing the library components would fail every pixel compare. Divergence is designer-visible here, not silently resolved.
